model.name: Fulfilment / Delivery
model.purpose: Represent how an external order or obligation is fulfilled by goods, services, digital content or access so agents can distinguish promise, allocation, preparation, dispatch, handover, receipt, inspection, acceptance, exception and completion without confusing fulfilment with shipment, inventory, invoice, payment, return or refund.
model.scope_statement: Owns fulfilment identity, versions, profiles and state; order, contract, line and obligation bindings; party roles and authority; promised product, service, resource, digital content, entitlement, specification, lot and serial references; fulfilment units, splits, batches, stages, packages and dependencies; ordered, promised, allocated, prepared, dispatched, delivered, received, accepted, rejected and outstanding quantities; substitution, tolerance, quality and condition assertions; plan, allocation, backorder, readiness, preparation, dispatch or activation evidence; shipment, consignment, carrier, transport and custody references; delivery attempts, handover proof, receipt, examination, inspection, conformity, acceptance and rejection evidence; shortages, excess, damage, loss, delay, failure, recovery, remedies, reconciliation, completion and discharge assertions; distinct clocks, provenance, privacy, retention, validation and loss-aware projections. External order, party, product, inventory, shipment, service, entitlement, invoice, payment, return and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Fulfilment identity, versions, obligation and party bindings, promised subjects, units, composition, quantities, conditions, allocation, readiness and dispatch or activation evidence
Handover, receipt, inspection, acceptance, exceptions, remedies, reconciliation, completion, clocks, provenance, access, retention and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Purchase Order, Contract, Party, Product, Service, Inventory, Warehouse, Shipment, Consignment, Package, Route, Location, Digital Artifact, Entitlement, Appointment, Work Order, Invoice, Payment, Return, Refund, Support or Records masters
Treating dispatched, delivered, received, accepted or completed status as universal proof of intended-recipient receipt, conformity, payment, discharge, risk transfer or dispute closure
Autonomous order acceptance, inventory allocation, dispatch, service activation, receipt signature, acceptance, discharge, invoicing, payment, return, refund, disclosure or physical disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The candidate ledger says the order contains fulfilment obligations. The order owns the exchanged commitment; this model owns obligation-performance and evidence context and does not mutate the order.
The candidate reference points to physical transport execution. Shipment, consignment, package, carrier, route and tracking remain external while fulfilment binds dispatch and delivery evidence.
The candidate reference connects delivered or accepted quantities to billing evidence. Fulfilment never issues or settles invoices.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Inventory, service execution, entitlement, return and refund
boundary_notes.distinction: These systems own allocation, actual service or access, reverse logistics and financial remedy lifecycles; fulfilment records typed references and effect observations.

boundary_notes.neighbor: UBL, UN/EDIFACT, EPCIS, CISG, EU law, Schema.org, TM Forum, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation has a distinct scope; every mapping is version-pinned, profile-qualified and loss-declaring.
